safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated radiation is documented to the left arm, but does not include shoulder/neck radiation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting shoulder/neck radiation may understate classic anginal features and slightly reduce perceived likelihood of ACS, though left arm radiation and ongoing central chest pressure were still documented and prompted EMS activation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state haemodynamic stability (it instead notes no vitals documented).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting hemodynamic stability removes a useful risk-stratification datapoint, but it would not typically change immediate management here because the patient’s symptoms already warrant emergency evaluation and vitals will be reassessed by EMS/ED.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient was examined while seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state patient was examined seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the patient was seated at rest during video inspection has negligible impact on diagnosis or emergency management for suspected ACS.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient appears well perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state patient appeared well perfused on video.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to note “well perfused” is a minor loss of clinical context; perfusion and circulatory status will be re-evaluated urgently by EMS/ED and does not materially alter the escalation already undertaken.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions ECG but does not include the need for troponin T testing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not explicitly stating the need for troponin testing could contribute to an incomplete ACS workup plan if acted on in isolation; however, EMS conveyance for suspected MI would almost certainly trigger troponins and serial ECGs in the ED.

safety_verdicts.content: Ambulance (LAS) was called with blue lights.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated states EMS/ambulance activation but does not specify blue lights/urgent response.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying “blue lights”/priority response is largely an operational detail; the key clinical action (calling an ambulance for ongoing chest pain suspicious for MI) was still documented.

safety_verdicts.content: LAS to clarify patient's other medications, which were not obtained.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not note that other medications were not obtained and EMS should clarify them.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient’s regular medications were not obtained can impair medication reconciliation and immediate decisions (e.g., antihypertensives, anticoagulants, PDE5 inhibitors relevant to nitrates), though EMS/ED typically re-collect this information.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold physical finding of 'not SOB' (even though SOB is mentioned in the transcript).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting shortness of breath when the gold standard says “not SOB” may inflate perceived acuity and bias risk assessment, but in this case the patient already had ongoing chest pressure with diaphoresis/nausea prompting emergency escalation regardless.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Not supported by gold (which lists physical findings) and is a meta-documentation statement not established as a clinical fact in the transcript.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating “no vitals documented” (when physical findings exist in the gold record) can mislead downstream clinicians about what objective data are available and may cause redundant assessment, but is unlikely to directly cause harm given EMS/ED will obtain vitals immediately.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Not supported by gold (which includes exam-based findings) and asserts absence of exam documentation rather than a patient/clinical finding.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating “no exam documented” can incorrectly imply that no assessment occurred and may reduce trust in the note or lead to repeat evaluations; however, it is unlikely to change urgent ACS management in an EMS/ED pathway.
